critics.name: spec
critics.intent: Does the diff do what the ticket and the brief ask, and does it do it correctly: missing or partial requirements, scope creep, and wrong behavior (false cache hits, exit codes, missed inputs, edge cases). It runs on every change.

critics.name: standards
critics.intent: Does the diff follow the documented repo rules (AGENTS.md of the repo and of the app, lessons-learned) and the smell baseline of the code-review skill. It runs on every change.

critics.name: simplicity
critics.intent: Is each part of the diff essential for the job, or accidental machinery: unused options, wrappers, fields and modes, and leftover analogue design. Spec-match is not a defense. It runs on every change.

critics.name: security
critics.intent: Trust surfaces: credentials and tokens, auth and organization isolation, OIDC and IAM trust, CI workflow trust (permissions, secrets, environments, triggers, third-party actions), sandboxes and egress, model routing to an outside provider, code that runs at install, at check listing or at check discovery (dependency scripts, bin entries, git dependencies), and data that leaves to a public artifact or an outside provider. A change that touches none of these is never a reason to run it; a workflow or package edit that does not change its trust is not one either.
notApplicable: no trust surface: the diff touches no credential, auth, CI workflow, IAM or infrastructure, install or discovery path, sandbox or egress, model routing, and no data that leaves to a public artifact or an outside provider
